You are doing design research for a real VPS/cloud-hosting company rebuilding its marketing homepage. FIRST call ToolSearch with query "select:WebSearch,WebFetch" to load the web tools.

Analyze the CURRENT (2026) live marketing homepages of: vercel.com, linear.app, stripe.com, railway.com (formerly railway.app), fly.io, cloudflare.com.

For EACH site, report concretely:
1. HERO VISUAL — what is it literally made of? Real product UI screenshot? Live interactive demo/embedded app? Rendered 3D? Abstract art? A terminal? A code block? Nothing (type only)? Be specific about what you can verify.
2. MOTION — what specifically animates, how much, and what is deliberately static. Named effects if you can find them (e.g. marquee, scroll-scrub, canvas particle field, video loop, autoplaying tab cycle).
3. TYPOGRAPHY — actual typeface names and pairings (search for "what font does X use", check their CSS/font files via WebFetch of their stylesheets if reachable, or design-teardown articles). Note how hierarchy is built (size jumps, weight, tracking, optical sizing).
4. TECHNICAL CREDIBILITY SIGNALS above the fold — real numbers with units, latency figures, region counts, customer logos, benchmark claims, uptime, code snippets with real syntax.
5. LAYOUT STRUCTURE — centered stack vs asymmetric/editorial grid; how sections are separated (hairline rules? background color shifts? full-bleed image breaks? bento grids?).

Methods: WebFetch each homepage (you'll get markdown — good for copy, headings, above-fold numbers, alt text, and sometimes inline style/script hints). ALSO WebSearch for recent design teardowns, "fonts in use", Typewolf/Fonts In Use entries, and dev commentary about each site's homepage. Prefer verifiable specifics over impressions. Mark anything you are inferring rather than confirming as "[inferred]".

Return findings DIRECTLY in your final message as dense structured notes. Do NOT write any .md files. Do not write code. Target ~700-900 words of pure specifics.

Research complete across all six sites. Findings below.

## VERCEL — vercel.com (fetched 2026-09-20)
**Hero:** Headline "Agentic Infrastructure"; subhead "For coding agents to ship apps and agents automated by agents." CTAs: "Deploy now" (→/new) + "Talk to sales". No code block, no terminal, no tabs in the DOM text. Visual is a **prismatic soft-focus gradient dispersing into geometric line patterns** on near-white — not a product screenshot [third-party measured].
**Type:** Geist Sans + Geist Mono (Vercel's own, open-source, drawn by basement.studio). Hero headline **weight 450** (not 600) at **-2.4px tracking**, sentence case. Mono is used for *eyebrows/labels only*: **11px / 400 / 0.071em / uppercase / #171717**. Hierarchy comes from weight restraint + huge tracking-negative display, not size alone.
**Layout:** Centered single column, ~1200px max-width, **visible rule-line grid** (Vercel's Geist `Grid` primitive explicitly treats cell borders/guides as design). Ink #171717 on #fafafa, ~200-step gray ramp, 6px radii on containers vs 9999px pill CTAs. No brand accent color — the ink *is* the brand.
**Credibility:** Notion "millions of agent conversations daily", Zapier "over 100 million monthly website visits", Mintlify "docs for over 20,000 companies". Named customers, not latency numbers.

## LINEAR — linear.app (fetched 2026-09-20)
**Hero:** "The product development system for teams and agents" — the string appears **three times in the DOM**, i.e. a layered/cycling text treatment [inferred]. Subhead "Purpose-built for planning and building products. Designed for the AI era." Announcement pill: "New — Loops →".
**Hero visual:** high-fidelity **real product UI** (Cloudflare-CDN images), incl. a genuine before/after code diff of `HomeScreen.tsx` refactoring sync-status handling — real TSX, not lorem.
**Type:** **Inter Variable** with OpenType `cv01` + `ss03` on globally. Weights 300 / 400 / **510** (signature emphasis weight) / 590. Display tracking scales: **-1.584px@72px, -1.408px@64, -1.056px@48, -0.704px@32px**. Code: **Berkeley Mono** → Menlo/Consolas.
**Palette/layout:** canvas **#010102** (deepest dark of the six), 4-step elevation ladder #0f1011 → #141516, hairline **#23252a**, single accent lavender-blue **#5e6ad2** reserved for CTA/focus. Screenshots in **16px-radius** panels; 96px section spacing. Sections: Intake and integrations → Planning and monitoring → AI and automations → Build, review, and ship → Changelog → testimonials (OpenAI, Ramp, Opendoor) → "Built for the future. Available today."
**Credibility:** "Linear powers over 40,000 product teams" + named-exec quotes. No latency/uptime numbers at all.

## STRIPE — stripe.com (fetched 2026-09-20)
**Hero:** "Financial infrastructure to grow your revenue." CTAs "Get started" + **inline "Sign up with Google"** (auth in the hero itself).
**Motion — the most technically documented of the six:** WebGL mesh gradient via **MiniGL**, ~800 LOC / ~10KB. Fragment shader uses **fractal Brownian motion** layering simplex-noise octaves, UVs warped by time-offset sin/cos. The canvas container is `transform: skewY(-12deg); overflow:hidden` — that's how the diagonal edge is made, not geometry. [Technique confirmed; continuity onto the 2026 page inferred.]
**Type:** **Söhne** (Klim, Kris Sowersby, 2019) shipped as one variable family `sohne-var` across marketing + Dashboard + docs; replaced Camphor. Display set at **light 300/400**, which is why it reads airy at huge sizes.
**Credibility — densest of all six:** 135+ currencies/payment methods · **US$1.9tn** 2025 volume · **99.999%** historical uptime · 200M+ active subscriptions · **500M+ API requests/day** · **10K+ req/sec** · **150K+ transactions/minute**. Logo rail is geo-swapped (Amazon, Google, NVIDIA, Toyota, Shopify, Figma, Anthropic, BMW; APAC visit adds Carousell, StarHub, GovTech).

## RAILWAY — railway.com ⚠️ *not directly fetchable*
Both `/` and `/home` **content-negotiate and serve an agent setup briefing** (pushing `curl -fsSL agents.railway.com | sh`) instead of marketing HTML. All below is third-party measured (snapshot 2026-05-13) + Railway's own changelog.
**Hero:** "**Ship software peacefully**" — confirmed by Railway's 2026-07-03 changelog "The peaceful way to ship software" and the railway.com/peace campaign (Martin Starr commercial, 5M YouTube / 12M X views).
**Hero visual:** full-bleed **hand-painted twilight/dawn scene** (clouds, mountains, a passing train) dissolving into flat near-black. Layered gradient violet **#3d2259** / pink **#291839** / far blue as "theatre lighting."
**Type:** **IBM Plex Serif, weight 500 only** — hero **54px / -1.96px tracking**; H2 40px/-0.8px; H3 36px/-0.72px. Body **Inter** 14/16/18/20; lede 18px/500/-0.09px. Stat eyebrows **Inter Tight 40px/600**. Code JetBrains Mono.
**Palette/layout:** canvas **#13111c** (indigo-midnight, tilts violet next to true black), elevated #1c1a28, ink #f7f7f8/#dcdce0/#a1a0ab. **One** violet CTA **#553f83**. Separation is **hairline #33323e** (1,049 occurrences — the dominant structural device); no cards, **no light surfaces, no white marketing bands, no polarity flips.**
*Conflict note:* a second scraper (Fudge) reported Inter / #0B0D17 / #7C3AED for Railway — generic-looking tokens, I judge it unreliable versus the specific set above.

## FLY.IO — fly.io (fetched 2026-09-20)
**Hero:** "Fly.io: computers for agents" / "Sandboxes aren't enough. Give your agent a real computer and get back to building."
**Credibility (hard numbers, above fold):** **18+ regions · <1s machine boot · 500ms typical deploy · 99.9% uptime SLA.** Real copy-pasteable terminal blocks in the flow: `curl https://sprites.dev/install.sh | bash` / `sprite login` / `sprite create my-sprite` / `sprite exec -s my-sprite -- ls -la`, and `curl -L https://fly.io/install.sh | sh` / `fly launch`. Logos: Supabase, Replicate, Builder.io, Firecrawl, Hatchet, Kilocode, Phonic, Plastic Labs, Steel, Delos, Lemonade.
**Type:** **P22 Mackinac** humanist serif at weight 500 — hero **64px / -2.88px tracking**; body **Fricolage Grotesque** [third-party]. Canvas near-white **#f1f2f9**, ink-violet **#281950**, CTA violet **#7c3aed**, 4-stop rainbow (cyan/indigo/pink/violet).
**Layout:** **the only asymmetric one** — text block in a center field with a separate illustration lane to one side. Section breaks are **Annie Ruygt watercolour illustrations** (dragons, fish, tools) in dusty pastels, not rules or color shifts. Reads as an illustrated periodical.

## CLOUDFLARE — cloudflare.com (fetched via /en-gb/; root served Workers-only content)
**Hero:** "Connect, protect, and build everywhere" + SASE/dev-platform subhead. CTAs "Start for free" + "See pricing".
**Above-fold stat strip (4 tiles):** **60+ cloud services · 234B cyber threats blocked each day · 20% of all websites · 335+ cities in 125+ countries incl. mainland China.** Logos: Discord, Zendesk, Investec, Broadcom, Colgate-Palmolive, DoorDash, Garmin, NCSC, Roche, Shopify, SoFi, US DHS, Thomson Reuters.
**Type:** **Inter** as sole typeface (Regular→Bold; Semibold does most emphasis, Bold reserved for display); **JetBrains Mono** for code [third-party]. White canvas, high-contrast dark type, single orange accent.
**Sections:** connectivity cloud → workforce/agents/apps → websites/AI apps → build & secure AI agents → "One global cloud network unlike any other" → "Leading companies rely on Cloudflare" → How we help → News → Get started. Separation is **background-color band alternation**, not hairlines.

## Cross-cutting takeaways for a VPS homepage
1. **Numbers-with-units above the fold is the infra norm** — Stripe (7 figures), Cloudflare (4-tile strip), Fly (4). Vercel and Linear deliberately use **named customers instead**. Railway uses **neither** — pure mood.
2. **Nobody uses abstract 3D.** The visual is either real product UI (Linear), a real terminal (Fly), an illustration (Railway, Fly), or a gradient (Stripe, Vercel).
3. **Display type skews light** — Vercel 450, Railway 500, Fly 500, Stripe 300/400, Linear 510/590. Heavy 700 display is the outsider tell.
4. **Tight negative tracking is universal** at display size: -1.6 to -2.9px at 54-72px.
5. **Two separation idioms only:** hairline rules on a single dark canvas (Railway, Linear, Vercel) or alternating light bands (Cloudflare, Stripe). Fly is the outlier with illustrated breaks.
6. **One accent color, rationed** — Railway #553f83, Linear #5e6ad2, Fly #7c3aed, Cloudflare orange. Vercel has none.

**Motion caveat:** WebFetch returns markdown, so animation is the weakest-confirmed dimension. Only Stripe's WebGL gradient is documented at implementation level. Railway's twilight-scene treatment, Linear's triple-rendered hero string, and Vercel's gradient behaviour are described structurally but their animation specifics are **[inferred]** — worth a real browser screenshot pass (Playwright) before you design against them.
